reason: planning stopped before any code was written: the critic judged that the reading misread the request: The reading says that all snapshot locking goes through `Snapshot::lock`. It does not: crates/athena-core/src/snapshot.rs has its own two-probe `lock` for the evidence snapshot the verifier reads. The request asks for the whole class to be fixed within crates/, so the reading's scope leaves out one instance of the same cause. (round 1 of 5). I read crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs (lock, probe_write, walk_one, set_write_bits, set_immutable, and the tests at lines 725-811), crates/athena-core/src/snapshot.rs (lock and probe_write at lines 127-169), verification.rs lines 195-346, CHANGELOG.md and docs/design/defaults-loop.md §3.7. The plan's claims about the code hold. `lock()` probes only a new file at the root and `.git/HEAD`. verification.rs:241-247 already turns a lock error into `Incomplete` before the verifier is invoked. The callers of `Snapshot::lock` are the ones the plan lists. Fixing this in `lock()` with an attempted write at every path is sound, and better than checking mode bits or adding more sample probes. Two things make the plan fall short, so the verdict is revise. (1) The tests build the partial lock from write bits only, which root ignores. The real component runs as root, as the job's own ~ working directory shows. Run as root, the lock-level test also passes against the old two-place probe: the old probe creates a file at the root, errors, and its message names the snapshot dir. The nested-path test passes trivially too, because as root every path is writable. So the "fails without the change" claim holds only for a non-root run, and only through compile failure. (2) The same two-place-probe lock is copied in crates/athena-core/src/snapshot.rs, for the evidence snapshot the verifier reads. The plan names it but defers it to the user. The request asks for the whole class to be fixed, and the scope is all of crates/. Findings: major: Run as root, the new tests also pass against the old two-place probe, so they do not show that the fix works for the user the real component runs as. (Demonstrations, criteria 2 and 3 (tests `lock_checks_every_path_and_names_the_writable_one` and `writable_paths_reports_a_nested_path_left_writable`); Risks bullet 4); major: A second copy of the same two-place-probe lock, the evidence snapshot's lock in athena-core, is left unfixed, so the whole class is not prevented. (Decision 5, second rejected alternative; Open question 1; crates/athena-core/src/snapshot.rs:133-169); minor: The CHANGELOG bullet blames the two earlier jobs on the two-place probe without evidence that the lock existed when they ran. (Step 5 (CHANGELOG bullet) and step 3 (doc comment)); minor: The test that no probe file is left behind runs only on an unlocked tree, not on the real lock path that the later tree comparison sees. (Demonstration for criterion 3, test (b) `an_unlocked_tree_reports_its_paths_and_leaves_no_probe_behind`); nit: The lock error cannot tell a path that accepted a write apart from a path that could not be checked.
